spec.name: xor_add_rot_chain_v1
spec.limitations: Byte-local only: no cross-byte mixing, so equal plaintext bytes stay equal under a fixed key and byte-frequency/repetition structure carries straight through. One known plaintext/ciphertext pair lets the full 256-entry table be read off and inverted, and nothing hides length or order. Rotation and modular addition also interact through carries, so there is no single cheap closed form and the map is not affine over Z_256.
spec.math: Every step is a bijection on Z_256: xor_key is x -> x XOR k; add c is x -> (x+c) mod 256; rol r is x -> ((x<<r) OR (x>>(8-r))) mod 256, i.e. rotation by r mod 8. A composition of bijections is a bijection, so the chain is exactly invertible: inverse = rol 2, sub_key (add (256-k)), xor 165, rol 5, sub 37, xor_key, applied in that reverse order with the same k.
spec.assumptions: Secret key byte k is fixed per challenge, uniform over 0..255, and substituted by the engine for each *_key placeholder whose operand (0) is ignored; public constants 37 and 165 and the rotations are known to the receiver; the inverse is run with the same k in reverse order.
